etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English nobody, no-body, no body. By surface analysis, no (“none, not any”, adjective) +‎ body (“one, person, individual”).

definitions.definition: Not any person; the logical negation of somebody.
Someone who is not important or well-known.

quote.citation: 1835, Charlotte Brontë, chapter XXVII, in Villette‎[1]:
quote.text: “‘The nobody you once thought me!’ I repeated, and my face grew a little hot; but I would not be angry: of what importance was a school-girl’s crude use of the terms nobody and somebody?”

definitions.definition: Something that has no body or an especially small one.
